'''Giacomo Candido''' (10 July 1871, in [[Guagnano]] – 30 December 1941, in [[Galatina]]) was an [[Italians|Italian]] mathematician and historian of mathematics.

==Education and career==
In 1897 Candido received his ''Laurea'' (teaching degree) from the [[University of Pisa]] and started to teach mathematics: first, at the Liceo of Galatina, then at the Liceo of Campobasso and from 1927 at the Liceo of Brindisi.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dm.unito.it/sism/m_italiani/biografie/tricomi/candido.html |title=Biografia SISM |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120717035131/http://www.dm.unito.it/sism/m_italiani/biografie/tricomi/candido.html |archivedate=2012-07-17 }}</ref>

He was an editor and contributor for the ''Periodico di Matematica per l'Insegnamento secondario'' and was one of the founders of the journal ''La Matematica elementare'' (an intermediate-level journal for teachers, engineers and students).<ref>{{cite book|author=Goldstein, Catherine|authorlink=Catherine Goldstein|author2=Schappacher, Norbert|author2-link=Norbert Schappacher|author3=Schwermer, Joachim|authorlink3=Joachim Schwermer|title=The Shaping of Arithmetic after C.F Gauss's Disquisitiones Arithmeticae|year= 2007|page=438|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IUFTcOsMTysC&pg=PA438}}</ref>

He was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1928 in Bologna<ref>Candido, G. "Applicazione delle funzioni U<sub>n</sub> e V<sub>n</sub> di Lucas all'analisi indeterminata." In ''Atti del Congresso Internazionale dei Matematici: Bologna del 3 al 10 de settembre di 1928'', vol. 2, pp. 17–24. 1929.</ref> and in 1932 in Zürich. In 1934 he founded the [[Apulia]]n branch of ''Mathesis'', an Italian association of mathematics teachers.

He is also remembered for his work on the history of mathematics.

==Candido's identity==
{{Main|Candido's identity}}
Candido devised his eponymous identity to prove that

<math> (F_n^2 +F_{n+1}^2 +F_{n+2}^2 )^2= 2(F_n^4 +F_{n+1}^4 +F_{n+2}^4 ) </math>

where F<sub>n</sub> is the ''n''th [[Fibonacci number]].<br />
The identity of Candido is that, for all real numbers x and y,<ref name=Alsina-Nelsen>{{cite journal|author=Alsina, Claudi|author2=Nelsen, Roger B.|title=On Candido's Identity|journal=Mathematics Magazine|volume=80|issue=3|year=2007|pages=226–228|url=http://www.lclark.edu/~mathsci/candido.pdf|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080705235056/http://www.lclark.edu/~mathsci/candido.pdf|archivedate=2008-07-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Koshy, Thomas|chapter=Candido's Identity and the Pell Family|title=Pell and Pell-Lucas Numbers with Applications|year=2014|page=169|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=j_9MBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA169}}</ref>

<math> (x^2 +y^2 +(x+y)^2 )^2= 2(x^4 +y^4 +(x+y)^4 ) </math>

It is easy to prove that the identity holds in any [[commutative ring]].<ref name=Alsina-Nelsen/>
